title: Project scaffold
description: Create the file-sharing crate within the p2panda workspace. This is a Bevy desktop app with egui for the UI, using p2panda for peer-to-peer networking.

spec.workspace_integration: Add "file-sharing" to the members array in the workspace root Cargo.toml.

dependencies.p2panda: p2panda-blobs (with fs-store feature), p2panda-core, p2panda-net — all via path deps
dependencies.gui: bevy (0.15, minimal features for windowed app), bevy_egui (0.34 for egui integration)
dependencies.async: tokio (full features), flume (mpmc channels for async bridge), futures-util
dependencies.serialization: serde (with derive), ciborium (maintained CBOR implementation, replaces serde_cbor), data-encoding (base32 for share codes), bytes
dependencies.platform: rfd (native file dialogs on macOS), directories (XDG/macOS app data paths)

spec.dev_dependencies: tempfile, iroh (with test-utils feature for dev relay), p2panda-net (with test_utils feature), tokio (with macros + rt-multi-thread)
spec.main_rs: Bevy App with DefaultPlugins (window title "p2panda File Sharing", 900x600), EguiPlugin, and a placeholder FileSharingPlugin. All module declarations in lib.rs.
spec.modules: node, bridge, manifest, share_code, protocol, share, download, persist, state, plugin, ui

Running the binary opens a native window with the correct title

title: Add download_with_progress to p2panda-blobs
description: The current Blobs::download() method awaits completion internally, discarding the byte-level progress stream from iroh-blobs. Add a method that returns the DownloadProgress handle so callers can consume the stream of DownloadProgressItem events, which include Progress(u64) for byte counts.

spec.new_method: Add an async method download_with_progress(hash) to Blobs that resolves the provider list from the address book (same as existing download()), then returns the DownloadProgress struct from iroh_blobs::api::downloader instead of awaiting it. The existing download() should be refactored to call the new method internally.
spec.re_exports: Re-export DownloadProgress and DownloadProgressItem from the p2panda-blobs public API so downstream crates don't need to depend on iroh-blobs directly.
spec.iroh_blobs_internals: The Downloader::download(request, providers) method returns a DownloadProgress struct. Calling .await on it runs complete() which drains the stream. Calling .stream().await instead yields a Stream<Item = DownloadProgressItem>. DownloadProgressItem::Progress(u64) gives cumulative bytes downloaded. DownloadProgressItem::Error reports failures. The downloader supports SplitStrategy::Split for multi-source parallel downloads via .buffered_unordered(32).
spec.backward_compatibility: The existing download() method must continue to work identically. Refactor it to call download_with_progress().await?.await? internally.

acceptance: cargo check -p p2panda-blobs compiles
Existing p2panda-blobs tests still pass
DownloadProgress and DownloadProgressItem are publicly importable from p2panda_blobs

title: Manifest format as signed p2panda Operation
description: Define the directory manifest that describes a shared directory's contents. The manifest is a signed p2panda Operation: a Header with the sharer's public key and Ed25519 signature, and a Body containing CBOR-encoded directory metadata. This provides cryptographic proof of who created the share.

spec.manifest_data_structure: A ManifestData struct with: version (u8, always 1), name (String, the directory's base name), and files (Vec of entries). Each file entry has: relative_path (String, forward-slash separated, relative to the shared directory root), size (u64, file size in bytes), and hash ([u8; 32], the iroh-blobs BLAKE3 hash of the file's content).
spec.cbor_encoding: Use ciborium for CBOR serialization of ManifestData. Provide encode and decode functions.
spec.operation_construction: Create a p2panda Operation with: Header (version=1, public_key from the sharer's PrivateKey, payload_size and payload_hash from the Body, timestamp from system clock as unix seconds, seq_num=0, no backlink, no previous, empty extensions) and Body (the CBOR-encoded ManifestData bytes). Sign the header with the sharer's private key.
spec.blob_serialization: The manifest is stored as a single blob. Define a serialization format that packs the CBOR-encoded header and the body bytes into one byte sequence with an unambiguous separator (e.g. 4-byte length prefix for the header, then header bytes, then body bytes). Provide serialize and deserialize functions.
spec.verification: On the download side, deserialize the blob, verify the header signature, and check that the body hash matches the header's payload_hash. Return both the authenticated public key and the decoded ManifestData.

acceptance: Unit test: create a manifest, sign it, serialize to blob, deserialize, verify signature, data roundtrips correctly
Unit test: a tampered body (modified after signing) fails verification
Unit test: a manifest with nested subdirectory paths encodes/decodes correctly

title: Share code format
description: A share code is a compact, human-copyable string that encodes everything a downloader needs to find and retrieve a shared directory. It is exchanged out-of-band (copy-paste, chat message, etc).

spec.contents: A share code encodes three fields: collection_hash ([u8; 32], the HashSeq root hash identifying the collection), node_id ([u8; 32], the sharer's Ed25519 public key for address book bootstrap), and relay_url (Option<String>, the relay server URL if the sharer is using one).
spec.encoding: CBOR-serialize the struct, then base32-encode (RFC 4648, uppercase, no padding) using data_encoding::BASE32_NOPAD, then prepend the prefix "p2p-".
spec.decoding: Strip the "p2p-" prefix, base32-decode, CBOR-deserialize. Return clear errors for invalid prefix, invalid base32, or malformed CBOR.
spec.topic_derivation: The gossip topic is derived deterministically from the collection hash: TopicId = Hash::new(collection_hash_bytes).into(). This is a helper function in this module so both share and download flows use the same derivation. The topic does not need to be encoded in the share code because it can always be recomputed.
spec.design_rationale: The share code is intentionally minimal. The sharer's node_id lets the downloader bootstrap into the address book. The relay_url enables NAT traversal. The collection_hash identifies the content. Everything else (manifest, file list, individual file hashes) is discovered after connecting.

acceptance: Unit test: encode then decode roundtrip preserves all fields exactly
Unit test: decode rejects strings without the p2p- prefix
Unit test: decode rejects invalid base32 and truncated data
Share codes are reasonable length (under ~120 chars for relay URLs, ~60 chars without)

title: Gossip protocol messages
description: Define the binary message format for gossip announcements. When a sharer publishes a directory, they announce the collection hash on the gossip topic so that subscribers (downloaders already on the topic) learn about the content.
inputs: p2panda-test-claude/src/protocol.rs (reference pattern: BlobAnnouncement with type-tag + hash + payload)

spec.message_format: A CollectionAnnouncement containing the collection_hash (iroh_blobs::Hash, 32 bytes). Binary encoding: one-byte type tag (0x01) followed by the 32-byte hash. Total: 33 bytes.
spec.encode_decode: Provide encode (to Vec<u8>) and decode (from &[u8]) functions. Decode validates minimum length and correct type tag.
spec.extensibility: The type tag byte allows adding other message types later (e.g. 0x02 for peer-has-content announcements) without breaking existing messages.
spec.pattern_reference: This follows the exact same pattern as p2panda-test-claude's BlobAnnouncement but carries a collection hash instead of a single blob hash.

acceptance: Unit test: encode then decode roundtrip
Unit test: decode rejects wrong type tag and too-short input

title: Node module with FsStore and persistent identity
description: A long-lived p2panda node that persists blob data and node identity across app restarts. Unlike the test-claude app which uses MemStore and generates a new key each run, this node uses FsStore for crash-recoverable blob storage and saves its Ed25519 private key to disk.
inputs: p2panda-test-claude/src/node.rs (reference pattern for component initialization order)
p2panda-blobs/src/blobs.rs (Blobs::new takes &Store; both MemStore and FsStore implement Deref<Target=Store>)
p2panda-blobs/src/lib.rs (FsStore re-exported when fs-store feature is enabled, which is the default)

spec.persistent_key: On first run, generate a new PrivateKey and write the raw 32-byte seed to data_dir/node.key. On subsequent runs, read the file and reconstruct the key. This gives the node a stable identity across restarts, which matters for address book entries other peers hold.
spec.fs_store: Use FsStore::load(data_dir/blobs).await to create or open the persistent blob store. FsStore implements Deref<Target=Store> so it passes directly to Blobs::new(&fs_store, ...). The fs-store feature is already the default in p2panda-blobs.
spec.component_initialization_order: Same as test-claude: AddressBook → Endpoint (with private key, optional relay URL, optional insecure cert verify) → MdnsDiscovery (always Active mode for the GUI app) → Discovery → Gossip → Blobs. All components except Blobs take address_book and endpoint clones.
spec.configuration: NodeOptions struct with optional relay_url and insecure_skip_relay_cert_verify flag. No per-topic binding: the node handles multiple topics over its lifetime.
spec.data_directory: Use the directories crate's ProjectDirs to locate the platform-appropriate data directory (~/Library/Application Support/p2panda-file-sharing on macOS).
spec.key_difference_from_test_app: The test-claude node is ephemeral (MemStore, random key per run, single topic). This node is persistent (FsStore, saved key, multi-topic). The node struct should not hold a topic_id since it handles multiple shares.

acceptance: Node starts successfully, creates data directory and key file on first run
Restarting with the same data directory loads the same private key (verified by comparing node_id)
FsStore directory exists at data_dir/blobs/ after startup
Node can join multiple gossip topics simultaneously

title: Async bridge between Bevy and Tokio
description: Bevy runs its own event loop on the main thread. The p2panda networking stack is async (tokio). Bridge them with a dedicated network thread running a tokio Runtime, communicating via flume channels. This is a well-established pattern for Bevy apps with async backends.

spec.architecture: Spawn a dedicated std::thread running a tokio::runtime::Runtime. The Bevy main thread and the network thread communicate through two flume channels: one for commands (UI → network) and one for events (network → UI). The Bevy side holds the command sender and event receiver as a Resource.
spec.command_types: ShareDirectory (with transfer id and directory path), StartDownload (with transfer id, share code string, and output directory path), CancelTransfer (with transfer id).
spec.event_types: ShareReady (transfer id, share code string, total bytes, file count), DownloadStarted (transfer id, directory name, total bytes, file count), FileDownloadProgress (transfer id, file index, bytes downloaded — this is the byte-level progress from iroh-blobs), FileCompleted (transfer id, file index), TransferCompleted (transfer id), Error (transfer id, error message string).
spec.transfer_id: A simple u64 counter assigned by the UI thread when creating a new transfer. Used to correlate commands and events.
spec.network_loop: The network thread initializes the AppNode, then enters a loop that selects on incoming commands from the channel. Share and download operations are spawned as separate tokio tasks so they run concurrently. Each task sends events back through the event channel.
spec.nonblocking_polling: The Bevy side uses try_recv() to drain all pending events each frame without blocking the render loop.

acceptance: Commands sent from the Bevy thread are received by the network thread
Events sent from the network thread are receivable via try_recv on the Bevy side
Multiple concurrent share/download operations can run simultaneously

title: Transfer state model
description: Bevy ECS resource tracking all active and completed transfers. Updated by the network polling system and read by the UI system each frame.

spec.transfer_registry: A Bevy Resource containing a Vec of transfers and a monotonic ID counter. Provides methods to allocate a new ID, and to look up transfers by ID (both shared and mutable references).
spec.transfer_struct: Each transfer has: id, name (directory name), direction (Upload or Download), status (Pending, Active, Completed, or Error with message), files (Vec of per-file progress), share_code (Option, set once sharing is ready), total_bytes, downloaded_bytes, start_time (Instant), and bandwidth rates for inbound and outbound data.
spec.file_progress: Each file tracks: relative path, total size, bytes downloaded so far, and a completed flag.
spec.progress_calculation: Transfer.progress_fraction() returns downloaded_bytes / total_bytes as f32 in [0, 1]. Bandwidth is calculated as downloaded_bytes / elapsed_seconds, updated each frame when new progress events arrive.
spec.direction_semantics: Upload means this node is sharing (seeding). Download means this node is fetching. Both are displayed in the transfer list with different icons.

acceptance: Structs compile and are usable as Bevy Resources
Progress fraction returns 0.0 when no bytes downloaded, 1.0 when complete

title: Share directory flow
description: The complete flow for sharing a local directory: scan files, import into blob store, create signed manifest, build a HashSeq collection, pin it, announce on gossip, and produce a share code. The sharer must remain online so peers can download blobs from them.
inputs: iroh-blobs Store API: add_path() streams a file from disk into the blob store (returns hash and size), add_bytes_with_opts() with BlobFormat::HashSeq creates a collection blob
iroh-blobs HashSeq: constructed from an iterator of hashes, serialized via into_inner() to Bytes, represents an ordered sequence of blob hashes
p2panda-blobs Pins: set(name, hash) pins a blob to prevent garbage collection

spec.directory_scanning: Recursively walk the directory. Collect each regular file's absolute path, relative path (from the shared directory root, forward-slash separated), and size. Skip hidden files (starting with dot), symlinks, and empty directories. Sort files by relative path for deterministic ordering.
spec.file_import: Import each file into the blob store using Store::add_path() which streams from disk without loading the full file into memory. This is essential for large files. Collect the returned hash and size for each file.
spec.manifest_creation: Build a ManifestData with version 1, the directory's base name, and the list of file entries with their relative paths, sizes, and blob hashes. Create a signed p2panda Operation from this data (task 3). Serialize the operation to bytes and import it as a blob.
spec.collection_building: Build a HashSeq from: [manifest_blob_hash, file1_hash, file2_hash, ...] in the same order as the manifest's file list. Import the HashSeq as a blob with BlobFormat::HashSeq format. The resulting hash is the collection root hash.
spec.pinning: Pin the collection blob to prevent garbage collection. Note: the current Pins API uses BlobFormat::Raw. For HashSeq blobs, use the underlying Tags API directly with BlobFormat::HashSeq to ensure the collection and all its referenced blobs are protected from GC.
spec.gossip_announcement: Derive the topic from the collection hash (task 4's topic derivation helper). Join the gossip topic via node.gossip.stream(topic_id). Publish a CollectionAnnouncement (task 5) with the collection hash. Keep the gossip handle alive so the node stays in the overlay.
spec.share_code_generation: Encode the collection hash, node ID, and relay URL (if any) into a share code (task 4). Send a ShareReady event with the code, total bytes, and file count.
spec.re_announcement: Periodically re-announce the collection (e.g. every 30 seconds) so peers who join the topic later discover the content.
spec.error_handling: If any file import fails, report the error but continue with remaining files. If the gossip join fails, report error to UI.

acceptance: Sharing a directory with 3 files (including a nested subdirectory) produces a valid share code
All file blobs, the manifest blob, and the HashSeq collection blob are present in the store
A gossip announcement is published on the topic derived from the collection hash
The share code decodes back to the correct collection hash and node ID

title: Download flow with byte-level progress
description: The complete flow for downloading a shared directory: decode the share code, bootstrap into the peer network, download the collection and manifest, then download each file with byte-level progress reporting. Supports crash recovery by skipping already-downloaded blobs.
inputs: p2panda-blobs Blobs: download_with_progress() returns DownloadProgress, .stream().await yields DownloadProgressItem::Progress(u64)
p2panda-blobs Blobs (via Deref<Target=Store>): has(hash) checks if blob exists, get_bytes(hash) reads complete blob content
p2panda-net AddressBook: insert_node_info(NodeInfo::from(EndpointAddr).bootstrap()) adds a bootstrap peer
p2panda-net iroh_endpoint: from_public_key() converts PublicKey to iroh NodeId, EndpointAddr::new().with_relay_url() builds address with relay

spec.share_code_decoding: Decode the share code to get collection_hash, node_id, and optional relay_url.
spec.peer_bootstrap: Convert the node_id to an EndpointAddr. If a relay_url is present, attach it. Insert into the address book as a bootstrap node. This tells the networking stack how to reach the sharer.
spec.collection_download: Download the HashSeq collection blob by its hash. Parse it into a HashSeq to get the ordered list of blob hashes.
spec.manifest_download: The first hash in the HashSeq is the manifest blob. Download it, deserialize the p2panda Operation, verify the signature, and decode the ManifestData to get the file list.
spec.file_download_with_progress: For each file in the manifest (corresponding to hashes at indices 1..N in the HashSeq): first check if the blob already exists locally via has(hash) — if so, skip it and emit a FileCompleted event (this is the crash recovery mechanism since FsStore persists to disk). Otherwise, call download_with_progress(hash) and consume the .stream() to get byte-level progress. Forward each Progress(u64) event as a FileDownloadProgress event to the UI. After download completes, read the blob content via get_bytes(hash) and write to the output directory, preserving the relative path from the manifest.
spec.directory_creation: Create parent directories as needed when writing files. Sanitize relative paths to prevent directory traversal attacks (reject paths containing .., absolute paths, etc).
spec.multi_source: The iroh-blobs downloader automatically contacts all known peers in the address book. If multiple peers have the same content (e.g. the original sharer plus another downloader who already has it), the downloader splits the request across them using SplitStrategy and buffered_unordered(32). No special handling needed — just ensure all relevant peers are in the address book.
spec.completion: After all files are downloaded and written, emit a TransferCompleted event.
spec.error_handling: If a single file download fails, report the error but continue with remaining files. Emit per-file errors so the UI can show partial completion.

acceptance: Downloads all files from a share code and writes them to the output directory with correct relative paths
Byte-level progress events (FileDownloadProgress) fire with increasing byte counts during each file download
Files in the output directory are byte-identical to the originals
Already-downloaded blobs (from a previous crashed run using the same FsStore) are skipped without re-downloading
Nested subdirectories are created correctly

title: Crash recovery persistence
description: Persist enough state to disk so that incomplete transfers can resume after the app exits or crashes. Blob data is already persisted by FsStore; this task handles the transfer metadata (which shares are active, which downloads are in progress, what share codes and output directories are being used).

spec.state_file: A JSON file at data_dir/state.json containing the list of active downloads and active shares.
spec.download_record: Each download record stores: share_code, output_dir path, and collection_hash. The list of completed files does not need explicit tracking because the download flow already checks blobs.has(hash) for each file — FsStore persistence handles this automatically.
spec.share_record: Each share record stores: source_dir path, share_code, and collection_hash. On restart, the share's blobs are already in FsStore; the app just needs to re-join gossip and re-announce.
spec.save_points: Save state.json whenever: a new share is created, a new download starts, a transfer completes (remove from active list). Use atomic write (write to temp file, then rename) to prevent corruption.
spec.startup_recovery: On app startup, load state.json. For each share record: re-derive the gossip topic, re-join, and re-announce the collection. For each download record: call the download flow which will skip already-present blobs and download only the missing ones.
spec.cleanup: When a transfer completes, remove it from the active list in state.json. Optionally unpin completed downloads' blobs after files are written to disk (the files are now on the filesystem, the blobs can be GC'd).

acceptance: state.json is written to data_dir after creating a share
state.json is written after starting a download
After simulating a crash (kill process), restarting the app resumes incomplete downloads
Shares are re-announced on gossip after restart

title: Transfer list UI with progress bars and dialogs
description: The main application UI rendered with bevy_egui. Shows a scrollable list of all transfers with real-time progress, plus dialogs for creating shares and starting downloads.

spec.main_panel: An egui CentralPanel with: a heading, a toolbar row with "Share Directory..." and "Download" buttons, a separator, and a vertically scrollable area listing all transfers.
spec.transfer_row: Each transfer is rendered as a group containing: a direction indicator (up arrow for upload, down arrow for download) and the directory name; a progress bar (egui::ProgressBar) showing downloaded_bytes/total_bytes with percentage text; a bandwidth display (formatted as KB/s or MB/s); a file completion count (e.g. "3/7 files"); and for uploads, the share code in a selectable text field with a Copy button that writes to the system clipboard via egui's clipboard API.
spec.share_dialog: When "Share Directory..." is clicked, open a native macOS folder picker using rfd::FileDialog. If a folder is selected, allocate a new transfer ID, add a Pending upload to the registry, and send a ShareDirectory command through the bridge. Show a brief "Importing..." status while pending.
spec.download_dialog: When "Download" is clicked, show an egui::Window with a single-line text input for pasting the share code. Optionally allow choosing an output directory (default: ~/Downloads/p2panda/). A "Start" button allocates a transfer ID, adds a Pending download to the registry, and sends a StartDownload command.
spec.status_display: Pending transfers show "Waiting..." text. Active transfers show the progress bar and bandwidth. Completed transfers show "Done". Error transfers show the error message in red.
spec.bytes_formatting: A helper function that formats byte counts as human-readable strings: bytes < 1024 as B, < 1MB as KB, < 1GB as MB, else GB.
spec.ui_state_resource: A Bevy Resource holding ephemeral UI state: whether each dialog is open, the current text input value for the share code field, the pending share path if a folder was just selected.

acceptance: Transfer list renders with correct progress bars and bandwidth for each transfer
Share dialog opens a native macOS folder picker and creates a transfer on selection
Download dialog accepts a pasted share code and starts a download
Copy button copies the share code to the system clipboard
Error states are displayed clearly

title: Network polling system
description: A Bevy system that runs each frame to drain all pending network events from the async bridge and update the transfer registry. This is the glue between the async network thread and the synchronous ECS world.

spec.polling_pattern: Use a while-let loop with try_recv() to drain all pending events non-blockingly in a single frame. This ensures the UI stays responsive even during rapid progress updates.
spec.event_handling: For each NetEvent variant, find the corresponding transfer by ID and update it: ShareReady sets the share code and marks Active. DownloadStarted sets the name, total_bytes, initializes file progress entries, marks Active. FileDownloadProgress updates the specific file's downloaded byte count and recalculates the transfer's total downloaded_bytes as the sum across all files. FileCompleted marks the file as done and sets its downloaded count to its full size. TransferCompleted marks the transfer as Completed. Error sets the error status.
spec.bandwidth_calculation: Each frame when progress events are processed, recalculate bytes_per_sec as downloaded_bytes / elapsed_seconds (from start_time). Only update when at least 0.5 seconds have elapsed to avoid noisy initial values.

acceptance: Progress events update the transfer registry within one frame
Bandwidth values are reasonable (not NaN, not negative)
All NetEvent variants are handled

title: Bevy plugin wiring
description: Wire all components together into a Bevy Plugin: spawn the network thread, insert resources, register systems in the correct order.

spec.plugin_build: In the Plugin::build method: determine the data directory using the directories crate, create flume channel pairs, spawn the network thread (which initializes the AppNode and enters the network loop), insert AsyncBridge, TransferRegistry, and UiState as Bevy Resources, and register the poll_network_events and ui_system as Update systems. Systems should be chained so polling runs before UI rendering.
spec.startup_recovery: During the network thread's initialization, after creating the AppNode, load the persisted state and resume any active shares/downloads. Send appropriate events back through the channel so the UI populates.
spec.main_rs_update: Replace the placeholder plugin with the real FileSharingPlugin.

acceptance: App starts without errors, shows the UI, network thread is running
Sharing a directory results in a share code appearing in the UI
Pasting a share code and clicking Start shows download progress

title: Integration test: local two-node directory transfer
description: End-to-end test verifying that a directory shared by one node can be downloaded by another node, with all files arriving correctly and byte-level progress events firing.

spec.test_setup: Create separate temp directories for: node A's data, node B's data, the source directory, and the output directory. Populate the source directory with test files of varying sizes and nesting: a small text file (~100 bytes), a medium binary file (~100 KB of random data), and a file inside a subdirectory (~500 bytes).
spec.node_setup: Create two AppNodes with separate data directories. Add node A to node B's address book using endpoint address information (same pattern as test-claude tests). No relay needed for local tests.
spec.share_and_download: Node A shares the source directory, producing a share code. Node B downloads using that share code into the output directory. Both flows use flume channels to capture events.
spec.verification: Walk the source directory and for each file, read the corresponding file from the output directory and assert byte-equality. Also verify that FileDownloadProgress events with increasing byte counts were received during the download.
spec.timeout: Wrap the entire test in tokio::time::timeout (30 seconds) to prevent hanging.

acceptance: All three test files (including the nested one) transfer correctly
Byte-level progress events are received during download
Test completes within 30 seconds

title: Integration test: relay-based transfer
description: Test that two nodes can share and download a directory when connected only through an Iroh relay server, verifying NAT-traversal capability.
inputs: p2panda-test-claude/tests/transfer.rs (test_relay_bootstrap_transfer pattern: run_relay_server(), relay_url, insecure cert verify)

spec.relay_setup: Start an in-process Iroh dev relay server using iroh::test_utils (same as the test-claude relay tests). This gives a relay_url for both nodes.
spec.node_setup: Both nodes are configured with the relay_url and insecure_skip_relay_cert_verify=true (since the dev relay uses self-signed certs). Node A is added to node B's address book with the relay URL attached to the EndpointAddr.
spec.transfer_verification: Same as the local test: share a directory from A, download on B via share code, verify all files match.
spec.relay_significance: This test proves the app works over the internet (not just LAN) by forcing all traffic through the relay. Without the relay, the nodes have no way to discover each other's direct addresses.

acceptance: Test passes: files transfer correctly via relay
No direct address exchange between nodes (only relay-mediated)

title: Integration test: crash recovery
description: Verify that a download interrupted mid-transfer can resume after restarting the node with the same FsStore data directory, without re-downloading already-completed files.

spec.test_scenario: Node A shares a directory with 3 files. Node B begins downloading. After the first file completes (verified by receiving a FileCompleted event for file index 0), drop node B entirely (simulating a crash). Then create a new AppNode for B using the SAME data directory (so FsStore retains the downloaded blob). Run the download flow again with the same share code.
spec.verification_criteria: The resumed download should skip the first file (blobs.has() returns true), download only the remaining files, and produce FileCompleted events for all files. The output directory should contain all 3 files, byte-identical to the originals. Verify that no FileDownloadProgress events were emitted for the first file during the second run (proving it was skipped, not re-downloaded).
spec.implementation_note: The crash recovery mechanism is inherent in the download flow: it calls blobs.has(hash) before each file download. FsStore persists completed blobs to disk. No explicit checkpoint file is needed for this test — the blobs themselves are the checkpoint.

acceptance: Second download run skips the already-completed file
All 3 files are present and correct in the output directory after recovery
No byte-level progress events for the skipped file during the second run

title: Integration test: multi-source download
description: Verify that a downloader can fetch content from multiple peers simultaneously, which is the BitTorrent-style swarming behavior enabled by iroh-blobs' Downloader.

spec.test_scenario: Three nodes: A (original sharer), B (first downloader who becomes a seeder), C (second downloader who should use both A and B as sources). Node A shares a directory with at least one large file (e.g. 1 MB) to make parallelism meaningful. Node B downloads the share from A completely. Then node C starts downloading the same share, with both A and B in its address book.
spec.multi_source_mechanism: The iroh-blobs Downloader's download() method accepts a list of providers (all node IDs from the address book). It uses SplitStrategy and buffered_unordered(32) to download different parts from different providers. Both A and B serve the same content, so the downloader can split the work. The key setup step is ensuring both A and B are in C's address book before C starts downloading.
spec.verification: All files on C match the originals. The download succeeds (proving multi-source works). Optionally, inspect DownloadProgressItem::TryProvider events to confirm both providers were contacted.
spec.design_note: This test validates that the architecture choice of using iroh-blobs (rather than a custom Merkle tree) still gives us the multi-source downloading behavior required for BitTorrent-style transfers.

acceptance: Node C successfully downloads from a swarm of two peers
Downloaded files are byte-identical to the originals
Test completes (proving the multi-source path works end-to-end)

title: Make sandboxed Rust verification environment reliable
description: Harden the local/docker sandbox workflow so PRD acceptance checks can run reproducibly for Rust tasks without manual apt installs or host-specific workarounds. This task exists because recent progress was blocked by missing linker/toolchain components, missing startup objects, and unreliable dependency fetching, which caused tasks to be marked passed without actually completing their feedback loops.
inputs: docker sandbox configuration or template build inputs used for codex-p2panda/claude-p2panda

spec.toolchain_baseline: Ensure the sandbox image or bootstrap script installs the full linker/runtime toolchain required by the configured Rust target, including gcc, mold, and the target's startup objects/libc development packages so linking no longer fails with missing Scrt1.o/crti.o errors.
spec.config_alignment: Either keep `.cargo/config.toml` aligned with tools guaranteed to exist in the sandbox, or adjust the config to use a linker setup that is actually present by default. The configured linker and rustflags must be valid inside the sandbox without manual intervention.
spec.dependency_fetching: Provide a reliable path for fetching crates in the sandbox, with documentation or scripting for cache reuse/prewarming where helpful, so new crates like Bevy can be resolved without ad hoc retries.
spec.verification_entrypoint: Add a repo-local command or script that runs cargo check/test inside the existing sandbox non-interactively. Do not rely on `docker sandbox run` launching the agent; use an explicit shell-command path such as `docker sandbox exec` against an existing sandbox.
spec.developer_workflow: Document the expected verification workflow: how to bootstrap the sandbox, how to run checks/tests, and how Ralph iterations should verify acceptance criteria once the environment is ready.
spec.non_goal: This task does not implement product features. It exists only to make task acceptance checks trustworthy and repeatable.

acceptance: Repo-local bootstrap and verification scripts exist for preparing and checking the Rust sandbox environment
The documented verification path uses a non-interactive sandbox command path and does not depend on launching the agent itself
When run in a prepared sandbox with required privileges and network access, `cargo check -p p2panda-blobs` succeeds
When run in the same prepared sandbox, a targeted `p2panda-file-sharing-gui` test command no longer fails due to missing linker or startup-object errors
docs/dev-environment.md explains the preparation assumptions the agent cannot guarantee itself

title: Recovered share display and status model rework
description: Fix recovered shares showing 'Recovered share' with 0/0 files after restart. Persist the directory name, file count, and total bytes in ShareRecord so recovered shares display identically to freshly created ones. Rework transfer status labels to use domain-appropriate terms: 'Seeding' for shares, 'Downloading' for in-progress downloads, 'Failed' for errors. Shares should show a 100% progress bar since the sharer has all data locally.

spec.share_record_fields: Add directory_name (String), file_count (usize), and total_bytes (u64) to ShareRecord. Populate them from ShareSession when creating a new record. Use serde default for backward compatibility with existing state.json files.
spec.recovery_event: In recover_startup_state, populate ShareReady events with the persisted directory_name, file_count, and total_bytes instead of hardcoded 0/0 values.
spec.transfer_name: When a ShareReady event arrives without a pre-existing transfer (recovery path), use the directory_name from the event as the transfer name instead of 'Recovered share'.
spec.share_status: When ShareReady is handled, set downloaded_bytes = total_bytes, mark all files as completed, and set status to Completed. The sharer has all data locally so progress should be 100%.
spec.status_labels: Change the UI rendering of status text: uploads with status Completed or Active display 'Seeding'. Downloads with status Active display 'Downloading'. Status Error displays 'Failed'. Downloads with status Completed display 'Done'.
spec.progress_bar_for_shares: Shares always render a progress bar at 100% (since downloaded_bytes == total_bytes). The progress bar remains visible alongside the 'Seeding' label.

acceptance: A fresh share shows the directory name, correct file count (e.g. '11/11 files'), 100% progress bar, and 'Seeding' status
After restarting the app, recovered shares show the same directory name, file count, progress bar, and 'Seeding' status as before restart
Downloads in progress show 'Downloading' status with the progress bar
Failed transfers show 'Failed' status with the error message
Existing state.json files without the new fields load without errors (serde defaults)

title: Per-share pause and resume
description: Allow pausing and resuming individual shares (both seeding uploads and in-progress downloads). Pausing a share stops all network activity for that share: leaves the gossip topic, stops serving blobs, and stops downloading. The paused state persists across app restarts. Each share has an inline pause/resume button in its transfer row.

spec.paused_status: Add TransferStatus::Paused variant. When paused, the UI shows 'Paused' label alongside the current progress bar (which stays at its last known position, e.g. 100% for a seeding share or 45% for a paused download).
spec.pause_command: Add NetworkCommand::PauseTransfer { transfer_id } and NetworkCommand::ResumeTransfer { transfer_id }. The network thread handles these by stopping or restarting the share/download activity.
spec.pause_seeding_share: Pausing a seeding share: abort the reannounce task, leave the gossip topic (drop the gossip handle), and stop serving blobs for that collection. The blobs remain in FsStore but are no longer announced or served.
spec.pause_downloading_share: Pausing an in-progress download: cancel the ongoing download task. Progress so far is preserved in FsStore (completed file blobs remain). On resume, the download flow restarts and skips already-completed files via the existing has()/completed_blobs mechanism.
spec.resume: Resuming a share: re-join gossip, re-announce the collection, resume serving blobs. Resuming a download: restart the download_share_with_progress flow which skips completed files.
spec.persist_paused_state: Add a paused boolean field to both ShareRecord and DownloadRecord. When a share is paused, persist it. On recovery, paused shares are not re-joined to gossip and their UI status is set to Paused. Use serde default (false) for backward compatibility.
spec.ui_button: Each transfer row gets an inline button: shows 'Pause' when the transfer is active/seeding/downloading, shows 'Resume' when paused. The button sends PauseTransfer or ResumeTransfer through the bridge. Disabled for failed transfers.
spec.independence: Per-share pause state is completely independent from the global app pause (task 22). Pausing share A does not affect share B. Global pause does not modify per-share pause flags.

acceptance: Clicking 'Pause' on a seeding share changes its status to 'Paused' and stops gossip announcements
Clicking 'Resume' on a paused seeding share resumes gossip and shows 'Seeding' again
Clicking 'Pause' on an in-progress download stops the download and shows 'Paused' with current progress preserved
Clicking 'Resume' on a paused download resumes from where it left off (skips already-completed files)
Paused state survives app restart: a share paused before exit remains paused after restart
Pausing share A does not affect the status of share B

title: App-wide pause and resume
description: A global toggle that pauses all network activity across the entire app. When active, all shares stop serving and announcing, all downloads stop fetching. The global pause does not modify per-share pause flags: when global pause is lifted, only shares that were not individually paused resume.

spec.global_pause_flag: Add a global_paused boolean to PersistedState (persists across restarts, serde default false). Add a corresponding flag to the UI state or a dedicated Bevy Resource so the UI can read it.
spec.toolbar_button: Add a 'Pause All' / 'Resume All' toggle button in the toolbar next to the existing 'Share Directory...' and 'Download' buttons. Shows 'Pause All' when unpaused, 'Resume All' when paused.
spec.pause_all_command: Add NetworkCommand::PauseAll and NetworkCommand::ResumeAll. PauseAll stops all active shares and downloads at the network level (same mechanics as per-share pause but applied to all). ResumeAll restarts only shares whose per-share paused flag is false.
spec.non_interaction_with_per_share: Global pause does NOT set per-share paused flags. It is a separate layer. When the user unpauses the app, each share checks its own paused flag: if the share was individually paused before the global pause, it stays paused. Only shares that were active before global pause resume.
spec.ui_indication: When global pause is active, all active transfers show 'Paused' status in the UI. Per-share pause buttons remain functional: the user can still toggle individual share pause state while the app is globally paused (the effect applies when global pause is lifted).
spec.persist: The global_paused flag is saved to state.json. On restart, if global_paused is true, no shares are resumed regardless of their per-share pause state.

acceptance: Clicking 'Pause All' stops all network activity and all transfers show 'Paused'
Clicking 'Resume All' resumes only transfers that are not individually paused
Scenario: share A is active, share B is individually paused. User clicks 'Pause All' then 'Resume All'. Share A resumes to 'Seeding', share B remains 'Paused'
Global pause state persists across app restart
Per-share pause buttons work while global pause is active (toggling the per-share flag)

title: Production-grade UI design review and overhaul
description: Review the current file-sharing app UI (see screenshot at file-sharing/Screenshot 2026-03-05 at 14.21.03.png) and redesign it to meet production-quality standards. This is a design-first task: analyze the current layout, typography, spacing, color usage, interaction patterns, and information hierarchy, then propose and implement concrete improvements following modern desktop app UI best practices.
inputs: file-sharing/src/state.rs (Transfer, TransferStatus, Direction — data model driving the UI)

spec.process: Begin by analyzing the screenshot and current ui.rs code. Identify all issues with layout, spacing, typography, visual hierarchy, color, iconography, responsiveness, and interaction design. Propose a concrete redesign plan with specific changes before implementing.
spec.scope: This covers all visual and interaction aspects of the egui-based UI: the toolbar area, the transfer list, the download dialog, progress bars, text formatting, button styling, spacing/margins, empty states, and overall layout structure. It does not cover adding new features — only improving the presentation and usability of existing functionality.
spec.quality_bar: The result should look like a polished, intentionally designed desktop application — not a developer prototype. Every spacing value, font size, color choice, and layout decision should be deliberate. Reference established desktop apps (Transmission, Syncthing, AirDrop) for appropriate visual patterns in the file-sharing domain.
spec.constraints: Stay within egui's capabilities. Do not add new crate dependencies for UI unless absolutely necessary. Prefer egui's built-in styling system (Visuals, Spacing, text styles) over custom rendering where possible.

acceptance: All existing UI functionality is preserved (sharing, downloading, progress display, share code copy)
Visual hierarchy is clear: the most important information (transfer name, status, progress) is immediately scannable
Consistent spacing and alignment throughout the interface
The app looks intentionally designed rather than using raw egui defaults
The UI works well at the default window size (900x600) and remains usable when resized

title: Global code review and architectural improvements
description: Perform a comprehensive code review of the entire file-sharing app codebase. The goals are: (1) ensure the code follows Rust and GUI app best practices, (2) improve architecture based on lessons learned during development, and (3) identify gaps in edge case and error handling. This is a review-and-refactor task, not a feature addition.

spec.process: Read every source file in the crate. For each file, evaluate: error handling (are errors propagated correctly, are edge cases covered, could panics occur in production), API boundaries (are public interfaces minimal and well-defined), module responsibilities (is each module cohesive, are there misplaced concerns), resource management (are files/connections/tasks cleaned up properly), concurrency (are channels, async tasks, and thread interactions sound), and idiomatic Rust (naming, types, patterns). Produce a list of findings grouped by severity (critical, important, minor), then implement the fixes.
areas: Error handling: unwrap/expect in non-test code, missing error propagation, swallowed errors, unclear error messages
Edge cases: empty directories, very large files, network disconnections mid-transfer, concurrent transfers, disk full, permission errors
Architecture: module boundaries and responsibilities, async bridge design, state management between bevy ECS and async runtime
Resource cleanup: graceful shutdown, temporary file cleanup, blob store consistency
Type safety: stringly-typed data that could use newtypes, missing validations at API boundaries
Testability: code that is hard to test due to tight coupling, missing test coverage for error paths
spec.constraints: Do not change external behavior or public APIs without flagging it. Preserve all existing tests. Keep changes focused — this is about correctness and maintainability, not style preferences.

acceptance: All existing tests pass after changes
No unwrap/expect calls remain in non-test production code paths (or each is justified with a comment)
Error types and messages are actionable — a user or developer can understand what went wrong and what to do
No resource leaks: temporary files, tasks, and connections are cleaned up on all code paths including errors
Module responsibilities are clear and documented where non-obvious
Edge cases identified during review either have handling or are documented as known limitations

title: Diagnostic view for network and app state inspection
description: Add a diagnostic view to the app that surfaces the internal state of the p2p networking stack and transfer engine. The primary use case is troubleshooting: understanding why transfers are slow, why peers are not connecting, or whether the node is healthy. This should answer questions like: Am I connected to other peers? Do I know about peers I'm not connected to? Were there connection errors? How long did connections take to establish? How much data has been transferred? Are there errors pointing at setup issues?
inputs: file-sharing/src/node.rs (AppNode with endpoint, address_book, gossip, blobs)

spec.view_design: A dedicated panel or tab in the app (not a modal) that can be toggled open. It should be always accessible, even when transfers are idle. The view should update in real time, not require manual refresh.

sections.node_identity: Node ID (public key), relay URL if configured, local listening addresses
sections.peer_connections: Table of known peers: node ID (truncated), connection state (connected/known/disconnected), how discovered (mDNS/relay/manual), time since last seen, current round-trip time if connected
sections.connection_history: Recent connection events: successful connects, failed attempts with error reason, time to establish connection. Capped ring buffer (e.g. last 100 events) to avoid unbounded memory growth.
sections.transfer_stats: Total bytes sent and received (all time for this session), number of active transfers, number of completed transfers, number of failed transfers
sections.error_log: Recent errors from the networking layer and blob store, with timestamps. Ring buffer capped at last 50 entries. Errors should include enough context to diagnose issues (e.g. 'failed to connect to peer X: connection refused' not just 'connection error').
sections.gossip_state: Active gossip topics, number of peers per topic

spec.data_plumbing: The async node (running on the tokio runtime) needs to expose diagnostic data to the bevy UI thread. Extend the AsyncBridge with a query/response mechanism or periodic diagnostic snapshots sent as NetworkEvents. Avoid polling the node on every frame — use a reasonable refresh interval (e.g. 1-2 seconds).
spec.constraints: The diagnostic view must not impact transfer performance. All data collection should be lightweight. The view should work even when no transfers are active. Do not expose sensitive data (full private keys). Truncate node IDs for readability but allow copying full IDs.

acceptance: The diagnostic view is accessible from the main UI via a toggle button or tab
Node identity section shows the node's public key and relay URL
Connected peers are listed with their connection state and discovery method
Connection failures are visible with error reasons and timestamps
Total bytes transferred (sent/received) are displayed for the current session
Recent errors are listed with enough context to diagnose networking issues
The view updates in real time without manual refresh
The diagnostic view does not cause noticeable performance degradation
All diagnostic data is bounded (ring buffers) to prevent unbounded memory growth

title: Cancel in-progress transfers
description: Allow the user to cancel a transfer that is currently in progress (either upload or download). Cancellation should stop all network activity for that transfer, clean up any temporary state, and update the UI to reflect the cancelled status. Partially downloaded data should be left on disk so a future re-download of the same share code can potentially resume.

spec.ui: Add a cancel button to each transfer row that is in Pending or Active status. The button should require a single click (no confirmation dialog — cancellation is not destructive since data is retained).
spec.cancellation_mechanism: Add a CancelTransfer network command. The async worker should use a cancellation token (e.g. tokio CancellationToken or a shared AtomicBool) to signal the running download/share task to stop. The task should check the token at natural yield points (between file downloads, during blob transfers).
spec.status: Add a TransferStatus::Cancelled variant. Cancelled transfers remain visible in the transfer list with a 'Cancelled' label.
spec.cleanup: On cancellation: stop sending/receiving blob data, leave already-downloaded blobs and completion markers on disk, release any temp pins. Do not delete the transfer from the registry.
spec.constraints: Cancellation should take effect within a few seconds — do not wait for a large blob transfer to complete before checking the token.

acceptance: Each in-progress transfer row has a visible cancel button
Clicking cancel stops network activity for that transfer within a few seconds
The transfer status changes to Cancelled in the UI
Already-downloaded files and blobs are preserved on disk
Cancelling one transfer does not affect other active transfers
The cancel button is not shown for already-completed, cancelled, or errored transfers

title: Remove completed and failed transfers from the list
description: Allow the user to remove transfers from the transfer list. For completed downloads this is cosmetic (hide from list). For completed shares (uploads), removal should also stop serving the share to other peers and clean up associated blobs and persistence records. This gives users control over what they are sharing and keeps the transfer list manageable.

spec.ui: Add a remove/dismiss button (e.g. X icon) to each transfer row that is in Completed, Cancelled, or Error status. For shares that are still being served, show a confirmation since removal stops serving.
spec.download_removal: Removing a completed download removes it from the TransferRegistry and the UI. Downloaded files on the user's filesystem are NOT deleted. Blob store data and completion markers may optionally be cleaned up to reclaim disk space.
spec.share_removal: Removing a share stops serving it: leave the gossip topic, unpin the collection and file blobs, delete the ShareRecord from persistence. The original source directory is NOT modified. After removal, the share code becomes invalid for new downloaders.
spec.bulk_actions: Add a 'Clear completed' action that removes all Completed transfers at once.
spec.constraints: Removal of shares must be confirmed since it is not easily reversible (the share code stops working). Removal of downloads and errored/cancelled transfers needs no confirmation.

acceptance: Completed, cancelled, and errored transfers show a remove button
Removing a completed download hides it from the list without deleting downloaded files
Removing a share stops serving it and deletes the persistence record
Share removal requires user confirmation
A 'Clear completed' bulk action removes all finished transfers at once
After removing a share, its share code no longer works for new download attempts
Active/pending transfers cannot be removed (they must be cancelled first)

title: System notifications for transfer events
description: Send native OS notifications when important transfer events occur, particularly when the app window is not focused. Users often start a download or share and then switch to other work — they need to know when transfers complete or fail without watching the app.

events_to_notify: Share ready: '{name}' is now available for download (share code ready)
spec.behavior: Notifications should only fire when the app window is not focused. Use the notify-rust crate (or equivalent cross-platform crate) for native OS notifications. Each notification should include the transfer name and a brief summary. Clicking a notification should bring the app window to the foreground if the OS supports it.
spec.rate_limiting: Do not spam notifications. If multiple transfers complete within a short window (e.g. 2 seconds), batch them into a single notification like '3 transfers completed'.
spec.preferences: No preferences UI for now — notifications are always on. A future PRD can add a toggle if users find them noisy.
spec.constraints: Must work on macOS, Linux, and Windows. Degrade gracefully if the notification system is unavailable (log a warning, do not crash).

acceptance: A native OS notification appears when a download completes while the app is not focused
A native OS notification appears when a share becomes ready while the app is not focused
A native OS notification appears when a transfer fails while the app is not focused
No notifications fire while the app window is focused
Rapid sequential completions are batched into a single notification
The app does not crash if the notification system is unavailable

title: Drag and drop folder to share
description: Allow the user to drag a folder from their file manager onto the app window to start sharing it, as an alternative to the 'Share Directory...' button and file dialog. This is a common desktop app pattern that makes sharing faster and more intuitive.

spec.interaction: When the user drags a folder over the app window, show a visual drop zone indicator (e.g. overlay with 'Drop folder to share' text and a highlighted border). On drop, immediately start the share transfer — same behavior as selecting a folder via the file dialog.
spec.implementation: Use bevy_egui's or winit's drag-and-drop event support. Bevy exposes FileDragAndDrop events from winit. Listen for these events in a bevy system and forward the dropped path to start_share_transfer.
spec.validation: Only accept directory paths. If a file is dropped instead of a directory, show a brief error message in the UI (e.g. 'Only directories can be shared'). If multiple items are dropped, share each directory and ignore files.
spec.visual_feedback: The drop zone indicator should be clearly visible — use a semi-transparent overlay covering the main panel. Remove the indicator when the drag leaves the window or after a drop.
spec.constraints: Must work on macOS and Linux at minimum. Windows support is desirable but not blocking if winit has limitations.

acceptance: Dragging a folder over the app window shows a visible drop zone indicator
Dropping a folder starts sharing it (same as the Share Directory button)
Dropping a file shows an error message instead of crashing or silently failing
The drop zone indicator disappears when the drag leaves the window
Multiple dropped directories each start a separate share
The existing Share Directory button continues to work unchanged

title: Content integrity verification display
description: Show the user that downloaded content matches what the sharer published by displaying hash verification results in the UI. This builds trust in the p2p transfer — users should be able to see that what they received is exactly what was shared, with no tampering or corruption.

spec.what_to_show: Each file in a completed download should display a verification status: verified (hash matches), or failed (hash mismatch or missing). The overall transfer should show an aggregate status: 'All files verified' or 'N files failed verification'. Show the content hash (truncated) for the overall collection.
spec.when_to_verify: Verification happens naturally during the iroh-blobs download — blobs are content-addressed, so a successful download implies the hash matches. The key information to surface is: (1) the download completed via content-addressed transfer (inherent integrity), (2) the collection hash that identifies this exact set of files. If a blob hash mismatch occurs during download, iroh-blobs will error — surface this as a verification failure rather than a generic error.
spec.ui_placement: In the transfer row, show a small verification badge or icon next to completed transfers (e.g. a checkmark with 'Verified'). In an expanded/detail view, show per-file hashes. The collection hash should be copyable (useful for out-of-band verification between sharer and downloader).
spec.for_shares: Shared directories should also show their collection hash, so the sharer can communicate it to the downloader for independent verification.
spec.constraints: Do not re-hash files after download — rely on iroh-blobs' content-addressing guarantees. The verification display is informational, not a separate verification pass.

acceptance: Completed downloads show a verification status (e.g. 'Verified' badge)
The collection hash is displayed and copyable for both shares and downloads
If a blob integrity error occurs during download, it is surfaced as a verification failure with a clear message
The verification display does not trigger additional disk I/O or re-hashing
Shares display their collection hash so it can be communicated to downloaders

title: Multi-platform packaging and release builds
description: Set up CI pipelines and packaging scripts to produce distributable application bundles for macOS, Linux, and Windows. Users should be able to download and run the app without installing Rust or building from source.

platforms.macos: Produce a .app bundle inside a .dmg disk image. Include an Info.plist with app name, version, icon, and bundle identifier. Sign with an ad-hoc signature at minimum (proper Developer ID signing as a follow-up). Support both x86_64 and aarch64 (universal binary preferred, separate binaries acceptable).
platforms.linux: Produce an AppImage that runs on major distributions without installation. Include a .desktop file and icon. Also produce a .tar.gz with the binary and a minimal README for users who prefer manual installation.
platforms.windows: Produce a .msi installer using WiX or equivalent. Include an app icon and start menu shortcut. Also produce a standalone .zip with the .exe for portable use.

spec.ci: Use GitHub Actions. Trigger release builds on git tags matching 'v*'. Build on native runners for each platform (macos-latest, ubuntu-latest, windows-latest). Upload artifacts to a GitHub Release. Include checksums (SHA-256) for all artifacts.
spec.versioning: Read version from file-sharing/Cargo.toml. The tag, Cargo.toml version, and artifact filenames must all agree.
spec.app_metadata: App name: 'p2panda File Sharing'. Set a proper app icon (create a placeholder if no icon exists yet). Include version info accessible from within the app (e.g. in the window title or an about dialog).
spec.constraints: Keep the CI workflow maintainable — prefer cargo-bundle, cargo-packager, or similar established tooling over custom scripts where possible. Build times should be reasonable (under 20 minutes per platform).

acceptance: A GitHub Actions workflow produces release artifacts for macOS, Linux, and Windows on tagged commits
macOS: a .dmg containing a .app bundle that launches on a clean macOS system
Linux: an AppImage that launches on Ubuntu 22.04+ without additional dependencies
Windows: a .msi installer and a standalone .zip that work on Windows 10+
All artifacts include SHA-256 checksums
The app version is visible within the application
Artifacts are automatically uploaded to a GitHub Release
